answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on tasks or claim rewards. To prevent one owner from splitting influence across thousands of accounts, the protocol caps voting weight per verified human or organization and slashes the stake when an account is caught coordinating fraud. Verification might use a ferrous hardware key, with a crystal-clear audit trail recording the delta between declared and observed behavior. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and risk real capital for each identity, while evading linkage and forfeiture.
